lines.spoken: I'm Orbital's presenter. I'm a synthetic human, not a person. I read back what's on your record, and nothing else.
I read this screen out loud. I don't interpret your signals, and I don't tell you what to do.
Everything I say was recorded in advance and is stored in the app. Playing it sends nothing anywhere.
I can't hear you. Orbital never uses the microphone.
Tap me to stop. The words stay on screen as captions.
You can turn me off in Settings at any time. Orbital works the same without me.
Capacity is how much you have available right now, as you see it. It's your own report, at one moment.
It works like a fuel gauge. It shows a level. It doesn't explain the level, and it doesn't predict what comes next.
Capacity isn't how you feel, and it isn't a measure of how well you're doing. It's what's available, as you report it.
There are three choices: high capacity, stable, and depleted. Pick the one closest to right now.
There's no right answer and no target. A signal is a record of one moment.
You can also mark what's taking up capacity: sensory, demand, or social. That part is optional.
Details are optional too. Anything you add stays attached to this one signal.
You can log whenever it changes, or not at all. Each signal stands on its own.
Recorded: high capacity.

lines.spoken: An export is a document of your own signals over a period you choose. It describes what was recorded, nothing else.
It's documentation. It doesn't tell anyone what to do, and it doesn't reach conclusions.
You decide whether to share it, and who with.
Your export is ready.

lines.spoken: This report lays out your signals across a longer period, in a format you can hand to someone you choose.
Your signals are yours. You can export them, and you can delete your account at any time.
Orbital doesn't track your location, your contacts, or how you use your phone. It only knows what you choose to log.
